According to the Organization for Small & Medium Enterprises and Regional Innovation's "Survey on Overseas Expansion of SMEs (2024)," 13.3% of companies are currently engaged in overseas expansion. Adding those with "plans" (2.1%) and "interest" (15.6%), approximately 30% are involved in or interested in overseas expansion in some form.
Key Points: While the figures vary depending on the definition and sample, the reality is that around 10% of SMEs actually operate overseas.

Among SMEs engaged in overseas expansion, "direct exports overseas" was the most common form of expansion at 44.4%. This was followed by "direct investment overseas" (39.8%) and "outsourcing production and sales to overseas companies" (38.3%). Cross-border e-commerce accounted for only 4.5%.

Currently, the most common overseas destination is "China (excluding Hong Kong and Macau)" at 58.6%. This is followed by "North America (USA and Canada)" (36.8%) and "South Korea" (33.1%). Meanwhile, "Vietnam" is the top destination for future expansion interest at 36.1%, followed by North America (28.7%) and China (27.4%).

Regarding the distribution of when overseas expansion began, companies that started before the 1970s accounted for 8.3%, while those that started in the 1990s (18.8%), 2000s (27.1%), and 2010s (27.1%) showed a gradual increase.

According to the Organization for Small & Medium Enterprises and Regional Innovation's "Survey on Overseas Expansion of SMEs (2024)," 13.3% of companies are currently engaged in overseas expansion. Adding those with "plans" (2.1%) and "interest" (15.6%), approximately 30% are involved in or interested in overseas expansion in some form.
Key Points: While the figures vary depending on the definition and sample, the reality is that around 10% of SMEs actually operate overseas.

Among SMEs engaged in overseas expansion, "direct exports overseas" was the most common form of expansion at 44.4%. This was followed by "direct investment overseas" (39.8%) and "outsourcing production and sales to overseas companies" (38.3%). Cross-border e-commerce accounted for only 4.5%.

Currently, the most common overseas destination is "China (excluding Hong Kong and Macau)" at 58.6%. This is followed by "North America (USA and Canada)" (36.8%) and "South Korea" (33.1%). Meanwhile, "Vietnam" is the top destination for future expansion interest at 36.1%, followed by North America (28.7%) and China (27.4%).
